name: PATN1 (leopard pattern)
summary: Pattern-1, the first established modifier of the leopard complex, associated with a variant in the 3' untranslated region of RFWD3 on chromosome 3. It sets how much white an LP horse shows and is dominant in that: UC Davis gives LP horses with PATN1 typically 60 to 100 per cent white, and those without it 0 to 40 per cent at birth; one LP copy plus PATN1 is usually a leopard or near-leopard, and LP/LP plus PATN1 a fewspot or near-fewspot. On a horse with no LP it does nothing and cannot be seen, so a solid horse can carry it and pass it on. It does not cause night blindness, which needs two copies of LP. Found in Appaloosas, British Spotted Ponies, American Miniatures, Norikers and Knabstruppers, where its frequency follows selection for extensive blanket and leopard patterns; no figure is published.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Carried, but silent on its own - it only shapes the pattern of a horse that also carries the leopard complex.
